```plato

    //==
    // # Marching cubes — the cube kernel
    //
    // One cube's worth of work, written against two sampling functions rather
    // than against a grid type, so that the dense grids, the sampled SDF and a
    // procedural field all share exactly this code.
    //
    // Sign convention: the extracted region is where the sampled value is AT OR
    // ABOVE isoLevel, and configuration bit c is set when corner c is BELOW it —
    // Bourke's convention, which is what makes his table's winding come out
    // counter-clockwise seen from outside that region.
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Winding, handedness, and normals.
    //
    // A field whose interior is the LOW side — every signed distance field, which
    // is negative inside — is marched by negating the sampled value, which the
    // SDF entry points below do.
    //
    // Corner samples are read again per cut edge rather than cached in an
    // eight-element array per cube. That is the cheaper trade at every grid size
    // worth marching: cut cubes are the surface, so their number grows as the
    // square of the resolution while the total grows as the cube, and the
    // overwhelming majority of cubes are uncut and pay only the eight reads the
    // configuration index needs. Caching would instead allocate on every cube,
    // including all of those.

    // The sampled value at corner `corner` of the cube whose minimum corner is
    // lattice node `cell`.
    MarchingCubesCornerValue(cell: IntegerVector3, corner: Integer, valueAt: Function3<Integer, Integer, Integer, Number>): Number
        => valueAt(
            cell.X + MarchingCubesCornerOffsetX(corner),
            cell.Y + MarchingCubesCornerOffsetY(corner),
            cell.Z + MarchingCubesCornerOffsetZ(corner));
```
